**Senior Director, Manufacturing Operations**

*Own the supply chain and CMC project engine behind Nurix's clinical programs and commercial readiness. In this multifaceted role, you will select and manage CMOs, keep clinical supply flowing to trial sites around the world, and drive cross-functional CMC plans from early development toward commercialization, in a small, entrepreneurial environment with broad responsibilities.*

  

**Position Description**

The position is a multifaceted role supporting several areas within the Technical Operations group, including supply chain management, CMC project management, and clinical labeling and distribution. The ideal candidate will be highly motivated and self-directed, with experience and interest in working in a small, entrepreneurial environment with broad responsibilities and opportunities.

  

**The Opportunity**

* Lead the effort to identify, select, and manage Contract Manufacturing Organizations (CMOs) for the development and cGMP manufacture of raw materials, RSMs, and DS in support of ongoing clinical programs and commercial products (with finance and commercial teams)
* Manage global supply chains and logistics in support of demand for clinical studies and commercial products
* Working in conjunction with technical teams, provide vendor management support in all logistics and operations to ensure on-time delivery of materials
* Coordinate the design and execution of cross-functional CMC project plans and budgeting for early clinical development through commercial readiness
* Maintain frequent communication with cross-functional CMC project team members and key internal stakeholders so that all parties are aware of current project status, issues, contingencies, milestones, and budgets
* Proactively identify the CMC critical path, risks, and impediments to successful development, and drive the identification and development of solutions to mitigate these risks
* Serve as primary clinical supply chain contact, working collaboratively with internal and external partners
* Manage clinical supply planning and forecasting for study protocols and develop packaging/labeling and global distribution strategies
* Monitor IXRS portal processes, including high and low enrolling site settings, drug acknowledgement, depot and site supply levels, and IMP status of released lots or expired drug
* Coordinate the preparation and/or review of CMC sections of INDs, CTAs, NDAs, MAAs, and other regulatory submissions to ensure timely distribution of clinical trial materials
* Coordinate the process validation programs to support commercialization
* Initiate and manage high-value intercontinental, cross-border, and domestic shipments
* Coordinate the preparation, review, editing, and approval of cGMP batch records and CMC regulatory and Quality documents
* Coordinate the preparation of technical reports, publications, and oral presentations

  

**What You'll Bring**

* BS with 15+ years' experience; degree in Pharmaceutical Chemistry, Organic Chemistry, Pharmaceutics, Pharmaceutical Science, or a related scientific discipline
* At least 10 years of relevant experience in a pharmaceutical or biotechnology CMC/cGMP environment
* Excellent project management skills and the ability to work cross-functionally to develop and execute project plans
* Experience managing US and international CRO/CMOs for the manufacture of raw materials, RSMs, and cGMP DS and DP for programs in development
* Experience with clinical supply chain, including forecasting supply needs
* Experience with cGMP manufacturing and IND, CTA, and NDA filings; thorough knowledge of relevant FDA and EMEA regulations
* Experience in supply chain management, and experience establishing pharmaceutical supply chain systems and networks
* Able to identify and resolve critical issues
* Sufficient technical background and experience to work closely with other technical functional areas
* Excellent written and verbal communication skills, and exceptional interpersonal and management skills to collaborate with others on assigned projects (including both internal teams and external collaborators)
* Bonus: Advanced degree in Pharmaceutical Chemistry, Organic Chemistry, Pharmaceutics, Pharmaceutical Science, or a related scientific discipline
* Bonus: Experience managing US and international CMOs for commercial programs

  

**Salary Range:** $270,300 - $295,700

*The posted range applies to roles based in the San Francisco Bay Area and reflects local market conditions. Where an offer lands within that range depends on the candidate's relevant experience, technical expertise, and how their background aligns with the role's requirements.*

  

**Location:** Onsite – Brisbane, CA

  

**Fit with Nurix Culture and Values**

* Strong team orientation; highly collaborative
* Solutions and results-oriented focus
* Hands-on approach; resourceful and open to diverse points of view

  

**About Nurix Therapeutics**

*Nurix Therapeutics is a clinical stage biopharmaceutical company focused on the discovery, development, and commercialization of targeted protein degradation medicines, the next frontier in innovative drug design aimed at improving treatment options for patients with cancer and inflammatory diseases. Powered by a fully AI-integrated discovery engine capable of tackling any protein class, and coupled with unparalleled ligase expertise, Nurix's dedicated team has built a formidable advantage in translating the science of targeted protein degradation into clinical advancements. Nurix aims to establish degrader-based treatments at the forefront of patient care, writing medicine's next chapter with a new script to outmatch disease.*

existing_roles.description:
**Director, New Product Introduction (NPI) & Product Lifecycle Management (PLM)**

Round Rock, Texas | Onsite | Full-Time

**Reports to:** CFO/CEO

**Works closely with:** Director of Operations/Engineering/R&D, Quality, Purchasing, Production, Program Management and external suppliers

**Travel:** Approximately 25%-35%, primarily to supplier locations

**Role structure:** Hands-on director role; initially an individual contributor leading cross-functional work

**Role Summary**

The Director of NPI & PLM leads the transition of new and modified products from development into stable production. The role coordinates product documentation, supplier readiness, pilot builds, production handoff and lifecycle changes across Ametrine and its manufacturing partners.

This position is focused on practical execution. The Director will work directly with cut-and-sew partners and other suppliers to ensure products can be produced repeatedly at the required quality, capacity and schedule. The role also helps develop alternate sources and contingency plans across fabric, metallization, printing, DWR treatment and cut-and-sew operations.

**Primary Responsibilities**

**New Product Introduction**

* Maintain the NPI schedule for new products, product changes and manufacturing transfers.
* Coordinate requirements, design release, sourcing, prototype builds, pilot production, validation and production handoff.
* Use clear stage gates, owners, due dates and readiness checklists.
* Identify schedule, supplier, material, quality and capacity risks early and drive actions to closure.
* Provide concise status updates covering progress, open decisions, risks and next steps.

**Prototype-to-Production Transfer**

* Work with Engineering and R&D to review designs for manufacturability and production readiness.
* Prepare or coordinate BOMs, routings, work instructions, technical packages, inspection points and packaging requirements.
* Lead prototype, pilot and first-production builds at Ametrine and supplier locations.
* Capture lessons learned and ensure changes are reflected in released documentation.
* Confirm that Operations and suppliers are ready before a product is released to routine production.

**Cut-and-Sew and Supplier Readiness**

* Work onsite with cut-and-sew partners to establish and improve production methods.
* Review patterns, sewing specifications, fixtures, templates, work instructions and inspection requirements.
* Assess supplier labor, equipment, training, floor space, quality controls and available capacity.
* Develop practical ramp plans and verify production rates through actual builds.
* Support supplier training and resolve manufacturability, throughput and quality issues during launch.
* Track supplier actions and escalate missed commitments or unsupported plans.

**Product Lifecycle Management**

* Maintain control of released BOMs, specifications, approved materials, suppliers, routings and product revisions.
* Coordinate engineering changes and assess their impact on inventory, suppliers, schedule, testing and customer requirements.
* Ensure the correct product configuration is used for each order and customer.
* Support PLM process and system improvements, including appropriate integration with ERP/MRP.
* Maintain orderly lifecycle records from product introduction through sustainment and retirement.

**Supply-Chain Resilience**

* Maintain a process-level supply-chain map covering fabric, metallization, printing, DWR, cut and sew, accessories and final delivery.
* Identify bottlenecks, long-lead items, single-source dependencies and supplier-capacity risks.
* Develop and qualify alternate sources where practical.
* Create contingency plans for specialized processes that cannot be economically dual-sourced.
* Coordinate source qualification with Operations, Purchasing, Engineering and Quality.
  

**Quality and Process Control**

* Partner with Quality to define process controls, inspection requirements and first-article expectations.
* Support supplier qualification, process reviews, root-cause analysis and corrective actions.
* Monitor first-pass yield, defects, rework and launch-related issues.
* Ensure production methods remain consistent with approved documentation and customer requirements.

**Cross-Functional Coordination**

* Lead NPI work through influence across Engineering, Operations, Quality, Purchasing and suppliers.
* Maintain clear owners, deadlines and escalation paths.
* Coordinate with the Director of Operations so new-product timelines and supplier readiness are aligned with the production plan.
* Support communication and coordination between Ametrine Inc. and Ametrine Ltd. where product development activities overlap.

**Success Measures**

* NPI milestones completed on schedule
* Prototype-to-pilot and pilot-to-production cycle time
* Supplier readiness and capacity verification completed before launch
* Percentage of critical supply-chain nodes with an alternate source or documented contingency
* Launch first-pass yield, rework and defect performance
* Completeness and accuracy of BOMs, routings, work instructions and product revisions
* Timely closure of supplier, manufacturing-readiness and lifecycle risks

**Required Qualifications**

* Bachelor’s degree in engineering, manufacturing, industrial technology, textiles, supply chain or a related field; equivalent directly relevant experience may be considered.
* Eight or more years of relevant experience in NPI, manufacturing engineering, supplier development, PLM, product transfer or contract manufacturing.
* Demonstrated experience moving physical products from prototype through pilot and into production.
* Experience working directly with external manufacturers or suppliers.
* Working knowledge of BOMs, routings, work instructions, engineering changes and configuration control.
* Experience with ERP/MRP and PLM or related product-data systems.
* Strong project planning, follow-through, problem-solving and written communication skills.
* Ability to work onsite in Round Rock and travel approximately 25%-35%.
* U.S. citizenship required due to the defense-related nature of the company’s work.

**Preferred Qualifications**

* Experience with technical textiles, sewn products, outdoor equipment, military products, automotive soft goods, medical textiles, inflatables or related manufacturing.
* Experience with cut-and-sew production methods, patterns, line balancing or labor standards.
* Experience with coated, laminated, printed or metallized fabrics.
* Defense, aerospace or government-contract manufacturing experience.
* Experience qualifying secondary suppliers or developing business-continuity plans.
* PMP, Lean Six Sigma, APICS or similar certification.

**Working Style**

* Hands-on and comfortable working at supplier facilities and on production floors
* Organized, practical and attentive to manufacturing details
* Able to communicate effectively with engineers, operators, supplier managers and company leadership
* Persistent in following actions through completion
* Comfortable balancing several product introductions and production issues at the same time
* Focused on building useful processes without unnecessary bureaucracy

**Why Build Your Career with Prysmian?**

**Your work at Prysmian helps power and connect the world.**

Prysmian, the world leader in solutions for energy and digital connections, strengthen its global team with the 2025 addition of Channell, now part of Prysmian. Founded by the Channell family in 1922, Channell brings a long‑standing legacy of innovation in outside plant infrastructure, serving Telecommunications, Municipalities, Internet Service Providers, Wireless, Water, Power, and CATV markets. Together, Prysmian and Channell team members are combining expertise, craftsmanship, and shared values to deliver a broader portfolio, from advanced cable systems and fiber connectivity solutions to enclosures and below‑grade vaults which support resilient infrastructure, the energy transition, and the growth of digital networks around the world.

When you join Prysmian, you become part of a global team whose work touches millions of lives every day. You’ll help support the energy and digital infrastructure that keeps communities, businesses, and industries moving forward.

For more than 140 years, Prysmian has helped shape the infrastructure that powers progress. From helping illuminate the Statue of Liberty in 1886 and delivering power from Hoover Dam to Los Angeles in 1935, to supporting New York City's rebuilding efforts after September 11, our cables and connectivity solutions have played a role in some of history's most significant milestones.

**What You’ll Bring:**

**Experience and Qualifications:**

* Bachelor's degree in engineering, operations management, business administration, or related field required; MBA or advanced degree preferred.
* 10+ years of progressive manufacturing operations leadership experience, including 5+ years leading multiple sites or a multi-plant network.
* Proven track record managing P&L, capital budgets, and operational KPIs across geographically dispersed facilities.
* Deep knowledge of Lean Manufacturing, Six Sigma, or comparable continuous improvement methodologies; certification (Lean/Six Sigma Green or Black Belt) preferred.
* Strong experience with ERP/MES systems and data-driven decision-making.
* Demonstrated ability to lead through others, build high-performing teams, and manage change across a diverse, multi-site organization.
* Working knowledge of OSHA, environmental regulations, and quality systems (ISO 9001 or equivalent).
* Experience in electronics, cable/connector, or precision component manufacturing a plus.
* Familiarity with thermoplastic molding - low and high pressure injection molding, rotational molding, and blow molding
* Willingness and ability to travel regularly (up to 40–50%) between facilities, including international travel as applicable.
* Executive-level communication and presentation skills, with the ability to influence senior leadership and the board.
* Strong financial acumen, including budgeting, forecasting, and cost analysis.
* Excellent problem-solving and decision-making skills in a fast-paced, multi-site manufacturing environment.

**What You'll Do:**

The Director of Operations provides strategic and operational leadership across the company's multi-site manufacturing network. This role is accountable for driving safety, quality, productivity, cost, and delivery performance at every facility while building a consistent operating system, talent pipeline, and culture of continuous improvement across locations.

The Director partners closely with Plant Managers, Supply Chain, Engineering, Quality, and HR to ensure each site operates at world-class levels and that capacity, capital, and talent decisions support the company's growth and customer commitments.

**ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS:**

* Develop and execute the multi-site manufacturing operations strategy in alignment with overall business goals, growth plans, and customer demand.
* Establish and standardize a common operating system (KPIs, daily management, tiered accountability meetings) across all plants to ensure consistent execution and visibility.
* Set annual operating and capital budgets for all locations; own P&L accountability for manufacturing operations.
* Drive productivity, throughput, and cost-reduction initiatives while maintaining or improving quality and service levels.
* Lead capacity planning, footprint strategy, and capital investment decisions across the network, including new equipment, line expansions, or facility consolidations.
* Directly manage and develop Plant Managers/Site Leaders at each location, setting clear performance expectations and holding sites accountable to targets.
* Build bench strength and succession plans for critical operations roles across all sites; partner with HR on talent acquisition, development, and retention strategies.
* Foster a culture of engagement, accountability, and continuous improvement; conduct regular site visits and gemba walks.
* Standardize best practices across facilities and lead cross-site knowledge sharing to eliminate performance variability between plants.
* Champion an EHS-first culture; ensure all locations meet or exceed OSHA and applicable regulatory requirements, with measurable reduction in incident rates.
* Ensure consistent adherence to quality management systems (e.g., ISO 9001) and customer quality requirements across all sites.
* Oversee compliance with environmental, labor, and applicable trade/export regulations at each facility.
* Lead deployment of Lean Manufacturing, Six Sigma, and/or Continuous Improvement methodologies across all locations.
* Drive standardization of processes, work instructions, and systems (ERP/MES) to improve consistency, data integrity, and decision-making across sites.
* Identify and lead major process improvement, automation, and cost-savings projects with measurable ROI.
* Partner with Supply Chain/Planning to align production schedules with demand, inventory targets, and on-time delivery goals.
* Collaborate with Engineering on new product introductions, process qualifications, and manufacturability improvements.
* Work with Finance on cost accounting, standard costs, and margin improvement initiatives.
* Partner with HR on workforce planning, labor relations, compensation strategy, and organizational design across sites.
* Serve as a key member of the senior leadership team, reporting operational performance and strategic recommendations to executive leadership and/or the board as needed.

**You’ll have the opportunity to make an impact, build strong partnerships, and grow your career in a business that values ownership, collaboration, and continuous improvement.**

**Total Rewards Designed for You:**

We believe great people deserve great rewards. That’s why Prysmian offers a total rewards package designed to support your financial, physical, and personal well-being now and as your career grows.

* **Competitive salary** that recognizes your skills, experience, and contributions
* **Performance-based incentives** that reward your results and impact *(where applicable)*
* **Comprehensive health coverage** with medical, dental, and vision plan options to fit your needs
* **401(k) retirement savings plan** with a competitive company match to help you invest in your future
* **Paid maternity and bonding leave, plus adoption assistance** to support you and your growing family
* **Generous paid time off and company holidays** so you can rest, recharge, and spend time on what matters most
* **Life and disability insurance** for added peace of mind
* **Wellness programs and supplemental insurance options** to support your overall health and well-being

**At Prysmian, you’ll be supported at work, at home, and throughout every stage of your career.**

existing_roles.description:
Kentucky Trailer

As a part of the global industrial organization Marmon Holdings—which is backed by Berkshire Hathaway—you’ll be doing things that matter, leading at every level, and winning a better way. We’re committed to making a positive impact on the world, providing you with diverse learning and working opportunities, and fostering a culture where everyone’s empowered to be their best.

Job Title: Director of Operations
  
Division: Kentucky Trailer  
Location: Louisville, KY- 3 site locations  
Reports to: President, Kentucky Trailer  
FLSA: Exempt  
  
This position has multiple direct reports across 3 sites. Current direct reports include Operations Manager, 7 Team Leaders, and a Manufacturing Engineer/Facilities Manager. This position requires local travel between the 3 sites in Louisville.  
  
Kentucky Trailer has been building in Louisville since 1879, when it was founded as the Kentucky Wagon Manufacturing Company. Today it designs and builds custom trailers and truck bodies for moving and storage, snack food distribution, package delivery, and specialty markets such as mobile medical, government, and motorsports. Most of what we build is engineered to order rather than off the shelf, which makes our operations both challenging and rewarding to lead.  
  
The Director of Operations leads all day-to-day manufacturing operations and is accountable for Safety, Quality, Delivery, Cost, People, and Productivity results. The role owns the manufacturing operating budget, develops frontline leaders, and builds a culture of accountability and continuous improvement. Works closely with Materials, Supply Chain, Engineering, Finance, Human Resources, and Commercial Sales to make sure production plans are executable and customer commitments are met. The workforce is non-union.

**Position Key Accountabilities:**

### **Safety**

* Create and sustain a Safety First and Always culture, with every employee understanding their personal responsibility for a safe workplace.
* Enforce safety policies, procedures and safe work practices at every level of the organization.
* Make sure hazards, near misses and incidents are addressed promptly, with root causes corrected.
* Ensure compliance with OSHA and environmental requirements and lead continuous improvement toward an incident-free workplace.

### **Manufacturing performance and planning**

* Lead daily manufacturing activities to meet production schedules and customer delivery commitments.
* Set clear daily, weekly and monthly expectations for each production area, and align labor and resources to requirements.
* Identify production constraints and implement corrective actions to improve throughput.
* Partner with Supply Chain and Materials so schedules are executable and escalate shortages before they affect production.
* Support point-of-use inventory, Kanban, vendor-managed inventory and other Lean material strategies where appropriate.

### **Quality**

* Build a culture where quality is owned at the point of manufacture and the next operation is treated as the customer.
* Ensure compliance with manufacturing standards, specifications, work instructions and quality procedures.
* Partner with Engineering to drive root-cause corrective action and reduce defects, rework, warranty exposure and cost of poor quality.

### **Lean and operational excellence**

* Champion Lean Manufacturing using 5S, Standard Work, Visual Management, Kaizen and structured problem solving.
* Establish a disciplined management cadence of daily production meetings, visual boards, KPI reviews and structured follow-up.
* Ensure standard work is documented, followed and continuously improved.
* Drive measurable improvement in labor productivity, cycle time, throughput, material flow, space utilization and manufacturing cost.
* Lead automation and capital initiatives that improve safety, quality, productivity and cost.

### **Financial performance and cost**

* Own the manufacturing operating budget and take part in the annual budget and monthly forecasts.
* Manage to labor, overhead and operating cost targets, including direct labor productivity, overtime and indirect labor.
* Ensure accuracy in both labor reporting and BOM usages
* WIP accuracy, and operational support for cycle counts and physical inventories.
* Partner with Finance to analyze manufacturing variances and carry out corrective actions.
* Prepare ROI justifications for capital requests and track whether completed projects deliver the promised return.

### **Maintenance and facilities**

* Ensure preventive maintenance programs maximize equipment uptime and extend asset life.
* Improve utilization of equipment, facilities and manufacturing capacity.

### **Leadership and people development**

* Lead, coach and develop managers, team leaders and employees across the operation.
* Set annual performance goals and development plans and hold leaders accountable for results.
* Build frontline leaders' capability in problem solving, waste elimination and employee accountability.
* Build organizational depth through hiring, succession planning and cross-training.
* Communicate regularly with employees about performance, company expectations, policies and priorities.

**Requirements**
----------------

* Bachelor’s degree in engineering, Manufacturing or another technical discipline, or equivalent experience.
* Minimum 10 years in manufacturing with a proven record of success and increasing responsibility.
* Minimum 5 years leading multi-site operations through managers and leaders.
* Demonstrated record of improving safety performance
* Lean Manufacturing experience or certification, with measurable results in efficiency improvement and cost reduction.
* Demonstrated P&L or operating budget accountability.
* Experience with ERP/MRP systems.
* Excellent written and verbal communication and problem-solving skills.
* Ability to manage multiple projects and priorities at once.
* Willingness to live and work in the greater Louisville, KY area.

**Preferred qualifications**
----------------------------

* Trailer, truck body or similar fabrication, welding and assembly experience.
* Experience in high-mix, custom build-to-order manufacturing.
* MBA or other financial education.

**Working conditions**
----------------------

This role works in both office and manufacturing plant settings, with exposure to noise, welding, painting and moving equipment. Required PPE must be worn on the production floor. The role regularly requires walking and standing for extended periods.

Employment is contingent on successful completion of a background check and drug screen.

CAMS is looking for a Plant Manager at the Kings Mountain Energy Center in Kings Mountain, NC. The incumbent will have 19 direct and indirect employees. The Plant Manager is responsible for the safe, reliable, compliant, and financially responsible operation and maintenance of the Kings Mountain Energy Center.

Kings Mountain Energy Center is a 475MW natural gas-fired combined-cycle power plant. The facility features an advanced 276MW Mitsubishi M501GAC gas turbine, a Vogt Power heat recovery steam generator (HRSG), a 225MW Toshiba steam turbine generator, and a Thermal Engineering International surface condenser.

The position provides overall leadership for plant operations, maintenance, engineering support, environmental and regulatory compliance, administration, workforce development, budgeting, outage execution, and continuous improvement. The Plant Manager serves as the primary site representative to CAMS leadership, facility ownership and asset management, and is accountable for developing a high-performing organization that maximizes plant availability, reliability, efficiency, and long-term asset value. The successful candidate will demonstrate strong leadership, sound technical and business judgment, and the ability to manage a complex combined-cycle generating facility in a competitive power-market environment.

### **Essential Duties and Responsibilities**

* Provide overall leadership and direction for the safe, reliable, environmentally compliant, and cost-effective operation and maintenance of the facility.
* Establish and maintain a strong safety culture in which employees and contractors actively identify hazards, stop unsafe work, and demonstrate personal ownership of safety performance.
* Ensure compliance with all applicable federal, state, and local environmental permits, laws, regulations, NERC requirements, OSHA requirements, company policies, and facility procedures.
* Lead and develop the plant management team and workforce, including recruiting, coaching, performance management, succession planning, qualification programs, and workforce development.
* Maintain effective working relationships with facility ownership, Asset Management, CAMS leadership, regulatory agencies, the system operator, utilities, OEMs, contractors, and other key stakeholders.
* Develop and execute annual operating plans, O&M budgets, capital plans, forecasts, and long-term maintenance strategies consistent with owner objectives and contractual requirements.
* Monitor plant financial performance and control expenditures while ensuring that short-term budget objectives do not create unacceptable safety, environmental, reliability, or long-term asset risk.
* Direct plant operations to achieve availability, reliability, heat-rate, start-reliability, capacity, and other performance objectives while meeting dispatch and commercial obligations.
* Provide leadership for maintenance strategies, preventive and predictive maintenance, corrective-maintenance backlog management, equipment reliability, root-cause analysis, and elimination of recurring failures.
* Direct planning and execution of combustion turbine, steam turbine, HRSG, generator, electrical, and balance-of-plant outages and major maintenance activities, including scope, budget, schedule, contractor performance, quality, and risk management.
* Develop and maintain multi-year outage, major-maintenance, and capital improvement plans based on equipment condition, OEM recommendations, operating profile, commercial requirements, and risk.
* Identify significant plant risks and provide CAMS leadership and ownership with timely information, alternatives, consequences, and clear recommendations for decision-making.
* Ensure appropriate critical-spares strategy, inventory controls, long-lead component planning, and equipment-obsolescence management.
* Oversee plant engineering and technical support activities, including equipment modifications, controls and logic changes, performance monitoring, capital projects, and technical problem solving.
* Ensure plant procedures, drawings, technical documentation, training materials, emergency plans, and operating records are accurate and maintained.
* Oversee administration of applicable plant contracts and agreements and ensure operational compliance with owner requirements, O&M obligations, OEM/LTSA requirements, fuel and utility agreements, and other commercial commitments.

**SUMMARY:** Directs production, distribution, maintenance, receiving, and supervision operations for the Plant, by performing the following duties personally or through subordinate supervisors.

**DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES:**

* Leads all departments in the plant with department supervisors (or production manager) to maintain safety, quality, and efficient production.
* Coordinates production, distribution, and warehousing in accordance with policies, principles, and established procedures.
* Develops and implements plans for efficient use of materials, machines, and employees.
* Reviews production costs and product quality and modifies production and inventory control programs to maintain and enhance profitable operation of plant.
* Directs preparation of production, human resources, and labor/costs records.
* Recommends budgets to management. Assists management in negotiation of employee contracts.
* Maintains positive working relationship with sales management and customer service management.
* Systematically reviews financial performance of the plant to recommend to management opportunities for sales growth and cost savings.
* Coordinates plant safety, environmental and training activities in cooperation with the Human Resources Department.
* Comply with company policies and procedures.
* Additional duties as assigned by management.

**SUPERVISORY RESPONSIBILITIES:**

* Manages subordinate supervisors and/or production manager who supervise all plant employees. Is responsible for the overall direction, coordination, and evaluation of these units.
* Carries out supervisory responsibilities in accordance with the organization's policies and applicable laws.
* Responsibilities include training employees; planning, assigning, and directing work; appraising performance; rewarding and disciplining employees; addressing complaints and resolving problems.

**EDUCATION and/or EXPERIENCE**:

* High school diploma or GED plus college and/or appropriate technical courses.
* Five years experience as a proven manager
* Ten years corrugated manufacturing experience
* Candidates are PREFERRED who offer the following:
* College degree

**LANGUAGE SKILLS:**

* Ability to read, analyze, and interpret general business periodicals, professional journals, technical procedures, or governmental regulations.
* Ability to write reports, business correspondence, and procedure manuals.
* Ability to effectively present information and respond to questions from groups of managers, clients, customers, and the general public.

**MATHEMATICAL SKILLS:**

* Ability to work with mathematical concepts such as probability and statistical inference, and fundamentals of plane and solid geometry and trigonometry.
* Ability to apply concepts such as fractions, percentages, ratios, and proportions to practical situations.

**REASONING ABILITY:**

* Ability to define problems, collect data, establish facts, and draw valid conclusions.
* Ability to interpret an extensive variety of technical instructions in mathematical or diagram form and deal with several abstract and concrete variables.

**TECHNICAL SKILLS:**

The individual must have a working knowledge of the following:

* Equipment design and capabilities that can be translated into efficient operation. This also supports the supervisor's role of teacher and trainer for his/her personnel.
* Cost issues in order to make daily decisions that will reduce overall costs and will help the supervisor find areas that require improvement.
* Budget development, adherence and analysis.
* Quality standards.
* Regulatory requirements including but not limited to wage and hour requirements, environmental and waste minimization, company policies, and personnel requirements including OSHA, DEQ and EEO.

**PHYSICAL DEMANDS**:

* The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the functions of this job.
* While performing the duties of this job, the employee is regularly required to talk or hear.
* The employee frequently is required to stand, walk, and sit.
* The employee is occasionally required to use hands to finger, handle, or feel; reach with hands and arms; climb or balance; and stoop, kneel, crouch, or crawl.
* The employee must frequently lift and/or move up to 100 pounds. Specific vision abilities required by this job include close vision, distance vision, color vision, peripheral vision, depth perception, and ability to adjust focus.

**WORK ENVIRONMENT:**

* The work environment characteristics described here are representative of those an employee encounters while performing the functions of this job.
* While performing the duties of this job, the employee is regularly exposed to moving mechanical parts.
* The employee is frequently exposed to wet and/or humid conditions.
* The employee is occasionally exposed to high, precarious places; fumes or airborne particles; and vibration.
* The noise level in the work environment is usually loud.

**LEADERSHIP ATTRIBUTES**:

The individual must posses the following:

* Superior time management skills including the ability to manage multiple issues concurrently and the ability to lead an effective and efficient meeting.
* Teaching skills in order to function effectively as a teacher for his personnel both in the technical and administrative parts of the position.
* Excellent crisis manager who demonstrates that he/she has a high emotional control under adverse conditions and can lead his/her personnel to a successful resolution.
* Excellent employee relations skills including being an active listener, understanding how to appraise personnel, applying both positive and corrective feedback, being able to resolve conflicts either involving the supervisor directly or as a third party, understands and demonstrates positive motivational skills including coaching and delegation techniques.
* Demonstrated confidence including providing a consistent leadership style with an acceptable level of professional assertiveness.
* Professional appearance to support his/her role as a managerial representative of the company.

**PERFORMANCE MEASUREMENTS**:

The performance of the supervisor will be measured as follows:

* **Operating standards** - the Plant Manager will need to see that all reporting staff meet or exceed the Operating Standards in the areas of quality, cost, safety, customer satisfaction and productivity. Such standards will be set annually and communicated to the supervisor.
* **Personal growth** - while the company will provide the tools to assist the supervisor to grow professionally the responsibility for moving forward lies with the individual. Each year there will be goals developed and agreed to by the supervisor and his/her superior.

**Employee relations** - through observations the Plant Manager will be evaluated regarding his/her and his/her reporting staff's skills and advancements in the areas of motivational techniques and results, positive and corrective/constructive feedback, subordinate development and creating a positive work environment.

**Carolina Container Company is an equal opportunity employer. We evaluate qualified applicants without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability, veteran status, and other legally protected characteristics.**

Job Duties & Responsibilities:  

* Establishing and maintaining production and shipping schedules and ensuring that quality

product is consistently delivered to customers on time and within budget for labor hours,
  
machine hours and material costs  

* Managing production operations such that equipment and employee resources are

utilized efficiently, productivity is high and product quality requirements are met and
  
exceeded  

* Ensuring that process and equipment capabilities meet or exceed company and industry

standards and requirements; implementing operations-related initiatives that result in
  
increased efficiency, improved productivity and reduced job-related costs

expected

equipment-related activities, ensuring that employees report labor hours, machine hours,
  
material usage and activities in accordance with company policies and procedures and
  
within the current operations management and control systems  

* Implementing operations and function-related budgeting goals and objectives;

establishing benchmarks for monthly, quarterly, and annual case production and
  
shipments, material receipts, production work-in-process completed and inventory levels
  
within the Plant Level of Operations

includes production, purchasing, shipping, receiving and inventory numbers as part of the
  
system of infernal checks and balances

accordance with company human relations policies and procedures

equipment maintenance

Executive Vice-President and President of the Company and supporting company policies,
  
goals, objectives, and initiatives  

* Ensuring that all product produced meets quality requirements in accordance with

company policy, procedures and requirements and in accordance with industry standards  

* Keeping the Management abreast of successes, progress and potential problems and

offering appropriate solutions for those problems  

* Simultaneously handling, prioritizing and resolving problems effectively
* Ensuring that shipment deadlines and budget and profitability objectives (i.e. gross margin

and operating profit) are met and exceeded on a quarterly and annual basis as established
  
by Director of Operations

hours per case, machine time per case, quality and cost per case; ensure that labor and
  
machine efficiency is within company guidelines; ensuring that periodic maintenance,
  
repair, rework hours and waste are within company guidelines  

* Ascertaining that purchasing, production support, shipping and receiving performance

metrics and objectives and inventory units and balance objectives are achieved or
  
exceeded on a quarterly and annual basis while ensuring on-time delivery of quality
  
product to customers at budgeted cost per case

industry

accordance with company procedures

supported in theory and followed in practice

make equipment, production and materials related decisions

dispatching, purchasing, shipping and receiving and inventory control functions using

* Outstanding communication skills with proven ability to successfully lead and develop a

team

and counsel while adding to the organizational climate and culture

positive attitude, service oriented, flexible, ethical, loyal and with high degree of integrity  

* Business maturity, team orientation and proven ability to positively influence change and

ensure business discipline through periods of growth while simultaneously protecting the
  
company’s operating principles and underlying entrepreneurial culture  

* Demonstrated good judgment in prioritizing, expediting, investigating and resolving

problems and issues and fosters harmonious relations with other company employees
  
while meeting and exceeding customer requirements  

* Respect for the confidentiality of company, customer, and employee information

growth; Solicits and applies customer feedback (internal and external); Fosters quality focus
  
in others; Improves processes, products, and services.; Continually works to improve

* Data-driven decision-making capabilities

At Pretium Packaging, we manufacture rigid plastic containers for some of the most recognized brands in the marketplace. Our plants operate with a strong emphasis on safety, performance, and continuous improvement.

existing_roles.title: Quality Systems Project Sr Manager
existing_roles.description:
At Zimmer Biomet, we believe in pushing the boundaries of innovation and driving our mission forward. As a global medical technology leader for nearly 100 years, a patient’s mobility is enhanced by a Zimmer Biomet product or technology every 8 seconds.

As a Zimmer Biomet team member, you will share in our commitment to providing mobility and renewed life to people around the world. To support our talented team, we focus on development opportunities, robust employee resource groups (ERGs), a flexible working environment, location specific competitive total rewards, wellness incentives and a culture of recognition and performance awards. We are committed to creating an environment where every team member feels inspired, invested, cared for, valued, and have a strong sense of belonging.

**What You Can Expect**
-----------------------

Leads the Quality Management System (QMS) integration of acquired medical device businesses and/or products into Zimmer Biomet (ZB) network. Plans, manages and executes the QMS Integration Project Plan (IPP) to update, harmonize and transition the acquired site’s QMS to ZB Global Quality requirements and applicable regulations; to remediate and transfer the site’s QMS and medical device product quality documentation and records from legacy systems into ZB global enterprise IT applications; and to ensure the site obtains and/or maintains certifications and establishment registration. Partners cross-functionally with Quality, Regulatory, R&D, Operations, Supplier Quality, Post-Market Surveillance, Servicing, IT, the Integration Management Office (IMO) and acquired-site leadership to complete integration on schedule and within budget while maintaining continuous regulatory compliance, product supply and in-process regulatory submissions.

**How You'll Create Impact**
----------------------------

* Leads cross-functional, multi-workstream QMS integration projects for newly acquired medical device businesses, from post-close planning through harmonization, documentation transfer, verification of effectiveness and integration closure.
  + Serves as the ZB Quality Integration Lead / QMS Project Leader for assigned acquisitions; accountable for the integration plan, schedule, budget, resources and deliverables.
  + Proposes corporate-wide process and issue solutions; resolves conflicts and escalates risks and roadblocks to Quality leadership and the IMO.
  + Coaches and mentors ZB and acquired-site team members on ZB Global QMS requirements; may supervise or direct team members, contractors and consultants.
  + Reviewer and approver of integration plans, gap assessments, migration protocols/reports and document-controlled forms.
  + Serves as Global SME for the QMS integration process and as site SME for multiple QMS sub-systems during transition.
  + Represents Quality in external and internal (global, site, IMO and executive) meetings, and during regulatory inspections and certification audits related to integration.
  + Strategic project planning for projects of all scale and complexity (plan, resources, budget).
* QMS Integration Planning and Project Management:
  + Translates due diligence findings into integration scope, risk-based priorities and workstreams; authors and maintains the QMS Integration Project Plan (IPP) per ZB global integration guidance and M&A procedures, and obtains cross-functional approval of the plan and its revisions.
  + Establishes and leads integration workstreams (e.g., Management Controls; Document & Record Controls & QMS Software; Design & Development Controls & Risk Management; Servicing; Purchasing, Production & Process Controls; CAPA / Quality Systems; Post-Market Surveillance; Regulatory and Clinical Affairs), assigning ZB and site owners, milestones and target dates.
  + Maintains detailed integration action plans, schedules and risk/issue logs (e.g., SharePoint, Smartsheet); leads recurring integration project meetings and reports status, budget, timeline, risks and roadblocks to Quality leadership, the IMO and site senior leadership.
  + Manages the integration budget and resource plan (including incremental headcount and external support) and revises the IPP when scope changes (e.g., new markets, new NPI projects, new product registrations).
* QMS Harmonization and Transition:
  + Leads gap assessments of site QMS procedures, processes and records against the ZB Global Quality Manual, global procedures (GBL/GBLW), and applicable regulations and standards; documents the harmonization approach and remediation actions.
  + Drives revision, adoption or retirement of the site Quality Manual, Quality Policy, procedures and work instructions; defines interim controls, “hybridized” processes, workstream decision forms and design control transition memoranda to maintain compliance until full adoption of global requirements.
  + Coordinates implementation of management controls, including Management Representative designation, organization charts and job descriptions, global KPIs and Global Quality Report, management review, and internal/external audit programs.
  + Establishes stakeholder-agreed cutover / go-live dates for each QMS sub-system (e.g., document control, CAPA, nonconformance, product holds, HHE/field actions, complaints, supplier controls, calibration, servicing) and ensures open legacy records are completed and closed under legacy procedures.
  + Coordinates intercompany quality agreements between the acquired site and ZB sites (e.g., complaint handling units, distribution and service centers) and contract manufacturers.

**How You'll Create Impact (cont.)**
------------------------------------

* Documentation Remediation and Transfer to ZB Enterprise Applications:
  + Plans and leads the transfer of QMS and product quality documentation and records from the acquired site’s legacy eQMS/document management system into ZB global enterprise applications (e.g., Windchill, OpenText LiveLink, WOW, Codebeamer, EtQ Reliance, iLearn, ServiceMax).
  + Develops data migration / transfer protocols, data mapping, acceptance criteria, verification and summary reports; ensures migrated and archived records remain complete, accurate, retrievable and compliant with record retention and electronic records/signature requirements.
  + Assesses and remediates product quality documentation, including Design History Files (DHF), Risk Management Files (RMF), Device Master Records, labeling, specifications and drawings, validations (process, software, test method) and supplier files (e.g., ASL, SPPA, SCN, SCAR), to ZB global requirements before or during transfer.
  + Coordinates with R&D and Regulatory Affairs to sequence documentation transfer so that ongoing NPI, design transfer and regulatory submissions (e.g., 510(k)) are not disrupted.
  + Partners with IT and global system owners on site set-up (e.g., site codes, user access, configuration), system training for site personnel, training curricula mapping to the ZB learning management system, and legacy system archival and decommissioning.
* Compliance, Effectiveness and Closure:
  + Ensures continued compliance and inspection readiness throughout the transition; initiates IE, CAPA or equivalent when gaps represent substantial noncompliance to regulatory requirements.
  + Supports site certification readiness (e.g., ISO 13485, MDSAP) and preparation for the post-integration corporate QMS audit.
  + Plans verification of effectiveness of integration activities (e.g., internal or independent QMS audit), drives closure of resulting nonconformances, and authors the IPP closure summary.
  + Captures lessons learned and continuously improves the ZB global QMS integration process, templates and playbook.

*This is not an exhaustive list of duties or functions and might not necessarily comprise all of the essential functions for purposes of the Americans with Disabilities Act.*

**What Makes You Stand Out**
----------------------------

* Expert knowledge of medical device QMS requirements: FDA 21 CFR Part 820, 21 CFR Part 11, ISO 13485, ISO 14971, EU MDR, MDSAP and other global regulations.
* Broad working knowledge of all QMS sub-systems: document and record control, design controls, risk management, CAPA, nonconformance, complaints/MDR, HHE/field actions, supplier controls, process and software validation, calibration, servicing and post-market surveillance.
* Proven program/project management of complex, multi-workstream, cross-functional projects (scope, schedule, budget, resources, risk and change control).
* Experience with M&A integration, site transfers/consolidations, or QMS harmonization and remediation.
* Hands-on experience with enterprise eQMS/PLM applications (e.g., Windchill, EtQ, OpenText, Codebeamer, Greenlight Guru), data migration and computer system validation.
* Strong knowledge of DHF, RMF, DMR and technical documentation content and structure.
* Ability to lead and influence without direct authority and to manage organizational change and cultural transition at acquired sites.
* Excellent executive-level communication, facilitation and status reporting.
* Sound risk-based judgement, problem solving and decision making in ambiguous, fast-changing environments.
* Excellent technical writing skills.
* Proficient with project management and reporting tools (e.g., MS Project, Smartsheet, SharePoint, Tableau/Power BI).

**Your Background**
-------------------

* Bachelor's Degree and 5 years of relevant experience, or Associate's Degree and 7 years of relevant experience, or High School Diploma or Equivalent and 9 years of relevant experience required.
* B.S. in Engineering, Life Sciences or related field preferred.
* Advanced degree (M.S./MBA) preferred.
* 10+ years in medical device Quality / Quality Systems or equivalent experience, including 5+ years leading cross-functional projects highly preferred.
* Experience leading QMS integration, harmonization or remediation for acquisitions, site transfers or eQMS/PLM implementations strongly preferred.
* PMP or equivalent project management certification preferred.
* ASQ CQA, CQE or CMQ/OE, or ISO 13485 / MDSAP Lead Auditor certification preferred.
* Lean / Six Sigma Green Belt or Black Belt preferred.
* Experience with SiMD/SaMD, robotics or capital equipment preferred.

**Travel Expectations**
-----------------------

* Up to 30% (domestic and international travel to acquired sites and ZB locations)

**Expected Compensation Range**
-------------------------------

$128,000 - $160,000 USD Annually

Shield AI is a venture-backed defense-tech company with the mission of protecting service members and civilians with intelligent systems. Its products include Hivemind autonomy software, V-BAT and X-BAT aircraft, and Aechelon simulation and synthetic reality technologies. With offices and facilities across the U.S., Europe, the Middle East, and Asia-Pacific, Shield AI’s technology actively supports operations worldwide. For more information, visit www.shield.ai. Follow Shield AI on LinkedIn, X, Instagram, and YouTube.

### **Job Description:**

Shield AI is actively seeking candidates with deep expertise in manufacturing and quality methodologies, paired with a relentless drive to enable supplier success and strengthen mission-critical operations.

Shield AI’s Supply Chain Quality team is responsible for global quality oversight across our supplier base. The team reduces supply-chain risk through supplier assessments and internal risk reviews, proactively drives supplier qualification and development activities.

In this role, you will lead a supplier quality team responsible for supplier qualification, development, performance management, and quality assurance across Shield AI’s aerospace and defense supply base. You will set supplier-quality priorities; manage team capacity, technical execution, and resource allocation; and develop high-performing quality leaders. The role also oversees supplier audits, nonconformance resolution, root-cause investigations, and hands on hardware dispositions.

You will evaluate supplier capability, quality performance, organizational risk, and resource needs to ensure purchased hardware and materials meet Shield AI engineering, customer, regulatory, and quality requirements. As an experienced aerospace quality leader, you will partner closely with Supply Chain, Engineering, Manufacturing, Operations, and Program teams to resolve complex supplier-quality issues, improve supplier capability, and reduce quality and delivery risk across the supply base.

* Develop the supplier quality team responsible for supplier qualification, surveillance, performance management, and corrective-action activities across Shield AI’s global aerospace and defense supply base.
* Establish supplier-quality priorities, allocate resources, and translate functional objectives into staffing, workload, and execution plans that support product, program, and organizational needs.
* Develop Supplier Quality leaders and engineering personnel through coaching, performance management, succession planning, workforce development, and technical mentorship.
* Oversee supplier qualification, risk assessments, periodic performance reviews, supplier audits, source inspections, and approved-supplier status across complex aerospace hardware, commodities, and manufacturing processes.
* Ensure supplier requirements are effectively flowed down and that suppliers comply with applicable quality management system, engineering, customer, contractual, regulatory, and statutory requirements.
* Escalate significant supplier-quality risks and direct SCARs, supplier recovery efforts, and capability-improvement plans that could affect product quality, delivery, mission readiness, or program execution.
* Partner with Engineering, Manufacturing, Operations, Supply Chain, and Program teams to address supplier producibility, design-for-manufacturability, process capability, technical execution, and quality risks.

* Understanding of ITAR, EAR, DFARS, and other requirements applicable to aerospace and defense suppliers.

* Proficiency with Microsoft Office applications, including Excel, PowerPoint, Word, and Outlook.

* ASQ Certified Quality Engineer (CQE), Certified Quality Manager (CQM), or equivalent quality certification.
* Six Sigma Green Belt or Black Belt certification.
* Experience leading supplier-quality functions in a high-growth aerospace, defense, autonomy, robotics, or advanced-manufacturing environment.
* Experience supporting the production and qualification of complex electromechanical, electronic, precision-machined, composite, or avionics hardware.

This position will directly impact the history of space exploration and will require your dedication and detailed attention towards safe and repeatable space flight! Join us in lowering the cost of access to space and enabling Blue Origin’s vision of millions of people living and working in space to benefit Earth!

  

Be part of the team of experts collaborating and leading overseeing a portfolio of projects to drive manufacturing evolution for Blue’s Engine Factory based out of Huntsville, AL. This role reports through the VP of Manufacturing.
  
  
We are looking for someone to apply their technical expertise, leadership skills, and commitment to quality to positively impact safe human spaceflight. Passion for our mission and vision is required!

existing_roles.title: Director, Industrial Engineering
existing_roles.description:
Anduril Industries is a defense technology company with a mission to transform U.S. and allied military capabilities with advanced technology. By bringing the expertise, technology, and business model of the 21st century's most innovative companies to the defense industry, Anduril is changing how military systems are designed, built and sold. Anduril's family of systems is powered by Lattice OS, an AI-powered operating system that turns thousands of data streams into a realtime, 3D command and control center. As the world enters an era of strategic competition, Anduril is committed to bringing cutting-edge autonomy, AI, computer vision, sensor fusion, and networking technology to the military in months, not years.

**ABOUT THE TEAM**
------------------

Anduril's Manufacturing Engineering Team is seeking a Director, Industrial Engineering to lead IE strategy and execution for the Air Defense & Strike (AD&S) division. The Manufacturing Team is responsible for rapidly iterating and building cutting-edge defense hardware — including static equipment, moving ground equipment, sensors, undersea, and flight vehicles — and scaling these products across our production footprint, including our new 5M sq ft manufacturing facility, Arsenal-1.

Industrial Engineering at Anduril operates in a matrix with a Center of Excellence (COE) and embedded IEs directly into the divisions they support. Every embedded IE takes day-to-day direction and priorities from their business line, while the central IE organization provides the methodology, standards, tools, mentorship, career development, surge coverage, and cross-divisional visibility that make each individual IE more effective than they could be on their own. The Director, IE — AD&S is the senior IE leader dedicated to one of Anduril's highest-growth, most operationally complex divisions — owning the IE strategy, team, and results for AD&S and operating as a peer member of the division's production leadership team.

**ABOUT THE ROLE**
------------------

As the Director, Industrial Engineering — AD&S, you will own the industrial engineering function for the Air Defense & Strike division end-to-end. You will build, lead, and develop the IE team embedded in AD&S — hiring the right people, designing the team structure, and setting the IE agenda in lockstep with the division's production strategy and ramp trajectory and COE standards and enterprise vision / system. You report to the Director of Industrial Engineering (central IE CoE) and sit as a peer alongside AD&S production leadership, connected to the VP of Production, Director of Manufacturing Engineering, and Program Directors who shape division priorities.

This is a division-level leadership role with enterprise accountability. You are not inheriting a mature, steady-state operation — AD&S is in active ramp across multiple product lines, standing up new production systems, scaling from prototype through low-rate into full-rate production, and doing so at a pace that demands IE leadership who can build the plane while flying it. You will define what IE looks like for AD&S: which capabilities to stand up first, how to staff and structure the team, where to invest in labor standards, layouts, simulation, and capacity planning, and how IE integrates into the division's NPI and production ramp cadence.

You will translate company-wide IE standards and the Manufacturing Development Plan (MDP) into AD&S-specific execution — adapting central methodology to the division's unique product mix, production maturity, and operational tempo while maintaining consistency with enterprise IE standards and Core 4 reporting. You are accountable for IE outcomes across the division: labor standards coverage, layout quality, line balance efficiency, capacity model accuracy, and the measurable impact of IE on AD&S production performance.

The right person for this role is a seasoned IE or manufacturing engineering leader who thrives in start-up and ramp environments — someone who has built teams from scratch, stood up production systems, and driven measurable operational impact in fast-moving, complex manufacturing. You have deep technical credibility in IE fundamentals but lead through strategy and people: setting vision, building organizational capability, and creating the systems that let a growing team deliver at scale. You are comfortable navigating ambiguity, making decisions with incomplete information, and operating at the intersection of divisional execution and enterprise IE strategy. You communicate with clarity and conviction to senior leadership and are energized by the challenge of building something new in a high-stakes environment.

**WHAT YOU'LL DO**
------------------

**Divisional IE Strategy and Execution**

* Own the IE strategy for AD&S — defining the roadmap, capability priorities, and investment plan aligned to the division's ramp trajectory, NPI pipeline, and business objectives.
* Translate company-wide IE standards and the MDP process into AD&S-specific execution — ensuring IE deliverables (labor standards, layouts, line balances, capacity models) are completed at the right maturity gates and integrated into division planning.
* Drive Core 4 metrics performance (labor hours per unit, line balance efficiency, throughput, units per square foot) — setting targets, tracking results, and ensuring IE work moves the numbers that matter to AD&S. IE provides the roadmap to scale.
* Serve as the primary IE interface to AD&S leadership for capacity questions, ramp feasibility, layout approvals, make-vs-buy analysis, and production system design. Connect AD&S needs to central IE capabilities and enterprise resources.

**Team Building and Leadership**

* Build the AD&S IE team into a high-performing, right-sized organization — designing the structure, defining roles, leading hiring, and onboarding IEs, IE Leads, and IE Technicians aligned to the division's product lines and production stages.
* Directly manage the embedded IE team — setting expectations, driving accountability, conducting performance reviews, and investing in the growth and career development of every team member. Own the headcount plan and budget.
* Develop high-potential talent, build succession depth, and ensure every IE is proficient in core methodology (time studies, MODAPTS/MTM, line balancing, layout design, capacity modeling, Core 4 measurement).

**Production System Design and NPI**

* Lead IE involvement in production line stand-ups and NPI ramps — from process characterization and layout design through labor standards development, line balancing, rate-readiness validation, and system optimization.
* Own production line and workstation layout design — cell configurations, material flow, equipment placement, and spatial planning for both low-rate and full-rate production using simulation-backed approaches.
* Drive capacity planning and production modeling — ensuring AD&S has accurate capacity models, proactively identifying bottlenecks and constraints, and supporting capital investment decisions with IE analysis.

**Cross-Functional Partnership and Communication**

* Operate as a peer member of the AD&S production leadership team — shaping production strategy, influencing capital and staffing decisions, and representing IE in all forums where production decisions are made.
* Build strong working relationships across Manufacturing Engineering, Supply Chain, Quality, Program Management, and Facilities. Represent AD&S IE in cross-divisional forums, bringing enterprise best practices back to the division.
* Be present on the floor. Walk the lines, build credibility with operators and supervisors, and model the Gemba-first, data-driven culture the IE team stands for. Communicate IE impact to senior leadership with clarity and conviction.

**REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS**
---------------------------

* Bachelor's degree in Industrial Engineering, Manufacturing Engineering, Systems Engineering, Operations Research, or a related field.
* 12+ years of experience in industrial engineering, manufacturing engineering, or production operations, with demonstrated depth across multiple IE disciplines (labor standards, layout design, capacity planning, simulation).
* 5+ years managing industrial engineers or manufacturing engineers, including experience managing managers or leads — with demonstrated hiring, org design, and team-building experience.
* Experience building or scaling an IE team in a ramp or start-up production environment — designing team structure, hiring into it, and standing up capabilities from early stages.
* Deep technical credibility in core IE fundamentals: time studies, labor standards (MTM/MODAPTS), line balancing, layout design, capacity planning, and production system design.
* Experience operating as a peer of production leadership — influencing strategy, owning budgets and headcount, and communicating IE impact to VP-level audiences.
* Track record of driving measurable operational improvement — IE initiatives that moved production metrics and can be quantified.
* Must be a U.S. Person due to required access to U.S. export-controlled information or facilities.

**PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS**
----------------------------

* Master's degree in Industrial Engineering, Manufacturing Engineering, Operations Research, MBA, or a related field.
* Experience in defense, aerospace, or other highly regulated, high-mix manufacturing environments with complex compliance and traceability requirements.
* Experience standing up a centralized or embedded IE function from scratch — methodology selection, standards development, tooling, and organizational adoption.
* Proficiency in simulation software (FlexSim, Arena, AnyLogic, or equivalent), data analytics/visualization (Power BI, Tableau), or experience integrating IE deliverables with MES/ERP platforms.
* Experience designing and commissioning new production lines or manufacturing facilities.
* Active security clearance, or ability to obtain and maintain a U.S. Secret security clearance.

The salary range for this role is an estimate based on a wide range of compensation factors, inclusive of base salary only. Actual salary offer may vary based on (but not limited to) work experience, education and/or training, critical skills, and/or business considerations. Highly competitive equity grants are included in the majority of full time offers; and are considered part of Anduril's total compensation package. Additionally, Anduril offers top-tier benefits for full-time employees, including:

  

### **Benefits**

At Anduril, we invest in our people. Our comprehensive, competitive benefits package (available at little to no cost to employees) ensures you're supported in health, recovery, and whatever comes next. *For more information,* *Explore Our Benefits**.*

  

### **Protecting Yourself from Recruitment Scams**

Anduril is committed to maintaining the integrity of our Talent acquisition process and the security of our candidates. We've observed a rise in sophisticated phishing and fraudulent schemes where individuals impersonate Anduril representatives, luring job seekers with false interviews or job offers. These scammers often attempt to extract payment or sensitive personal information.

To ensure your safety and help you navigate your job search with confidence, please keep the following critical points in mind:

* **No Financial Requests:** Anduril will never solicit payment or demand personal financial details (such as banking information, credit card numbers, or social security numbers) at any stage of our hiring process. Our legitimate recruitment is entirely free for candidates.
* **Please always verify communications:**
  + Direct from Anduril: If you receive an email from one of our recruiters, it will *only* come from an @anduril.com address.
  + Via Agency Partner: If contacted by a recruiting agency for an Anduril role, their email will clearly identify their agency. If you suspect any suspicious activity, please verify the agency's authenticity by reaching out to contact@anduril.com.
* **Exercise Caution with Unsolicited Outreach:** If you receive any communication that appears suspicious, contains grammatical errors, or makes unusual requests, do not engage. Always confirm the sender's email domain is @anduril.com before providing any personal information or clicking on links.
* **What to Do If You Suspect Fraud:** Should you encounter any questionable or fraudulent outreach claiming to be from Anduril, please report it immediately to contact@anduril.com. Your proactive caution is invaluable in protecting your personal information and upholding the security and trustworthiness of our recruitment efforts.

### **Data Privacy**

To view Anduril's candidate data privacy policy, please visit https://anduril.com/applicant-privacy-notice/.

  

By submitting your application, you consent to Anduril Industries using a third-party service provider to conduct pre-employment risk, integrity, and due diligence screening and assessing potential risks as part of your application process. This third-party service provider provides risk-intelligence services that may include analysis of sanctions and watchlists, adverse media, public-record information, and other lawful open-source or commercial data sources. This third-party service provider does not act as a consumer reporting agency. Use of this provider helps to ensure compliance with applicable laws and protect technology, intellectual property, and organizational security.

**About Carrier**

Carrier Global Corporation, global leader in intelligent climate and energy solutions, is committed to creating innovations that bring comfort, safety and sustainability to life. Through cutting-edge advancements in climate solutions such as temperature control, air quality and transportation, we improve lives, empower critical industries and ensure safe transport of food, lifesaving medicines and more. Since inventing modern air conditioning in 1902, we lead with purpose: enhancing the lives we live and the world we share. We continue to lead because of our world-class, inclusive workforce that puts the customer at the center of everything we do. For more information, visit corporate.carrier.com or follow on Carrier social media at @Carrier.

**About the Job**
-----------------

The Senior Manager, LCML Fulfillment Operations leads the end-to-end order fulfillment and distribution execution operating model for Carrier's Light Commercial (LCML) HVAC business within Climate Solutions Americas (CSA). Reporting to CSA Logistics & Supply Chain leadership, this role balances customer service reliability, on-time in-full (OTIF) delivery performance, inventory allocation governance, and fulfillment cost-to-serve productivity across North America.

This leader directs a team of fulfillment operations planners, order management specialists, and execution coordinators, steering initiatives in order backlog reduction, multi-site distribution throughput, order consolidation, and peak seasonal readiness. Working collaboratively with Light Commercial SIOP, Manufacturing Operations, Distribution Center (DC) Operations, Transportation, and Commercial Sales leadership, the Senior Manager establishes fulfillment KPIs and SLAs, enhances ERP/WMS/TMS data integrity, and champions continuous improvement across the order-to-delivery ecosystem.

**Work Arrangement:** Hybrid: 3 days in office at the Atlanta Digital Hub, 2 days remote per week.

**Key Responsibilities**
------------------------

* **Fulfillment Execution & Planning Governance:** Lead, mentor, and develop a high-performing team of fulfillment planners and execution coordinators managing day-to-day order allocation, scheduling, and customer delivery execution across North American distribution networks.
* **Network Throughput & Cost-to-Serve Productivity:** Drive order consolidation programs, warehouse/fulfillment cycle-time reductions, avoidable expedite elimination, and measurable cost-to-serve efficiencies across LCML distribution hubs.

Working in the Office of the Chief Medical Officer and reporting to the VP of Point of Care & Risk Stratification, the Senior Director of Strategy & Operations, Point of Care, will lead day-to-day operations, partnerships, go-to-market efforts, and wraparound support services to maximize the impact of Aledade’s value-based care insights to our partner practices.

The team is looking for a high-output generalist with a strong business analyst toolkit, looking to rapidly take ownership of complex content with high visibility, working across multiple stakeholders. Candidates that thrive managing multiple deadlines on tight timelines and learning content quickly are best positioned to succeed; successful team members in the same function primarily have backgrounds in consulting and generalist healthcare strategy & operations roles.

To start, the role will focus on 1) scaling the deployment of our point of care tools and 2) broadening and deepening the insights available in our point of care tools, to maximize the impact of Aledade’s insights on our patients’ health outcomes and partner practices’ success in their value-based care contracts.

At the end of their first year, a successful leader in the role will own end-to-end accountability for 1) proactive identification, development, and execution of Point of Care deployment improvement opportunities, including field, practice, and clinician education, deployment automation and monitoring, and go to market approach and materials, 2) strategic relationship building and partnership with Aledade’s payer partners to advance point of care tool adoption and impact, 3) goal setting, metric identification and development, and impact evaluation for our point of care tools, 4) identification, evaluation, contracting, and cross-functional execution of net new vendor and external partnerships that support insight delivery and impact.

Additionally, this role will 1) provide direction and expert guidance to junior team members owning individual initiatives, including incentive and adoption programs, educational efforts, hotspotting, monitoring, and alerting development, practice and user-level prioritization and triage, and 2) coordinate with cross-functional product, analytics, technology, performance, care programs, and other senior leaders across Aledade to advance point of care tool adoption and impact.

The role is expected to start as a senior individual contributor, but is expected to grow into a people manager in the near term.

### **Primary Duties:**

* Lead strategic relationship building and partnership with Aledade’s payer partners to advance point of care tool adoption and impact
